description: ocsp.rs line 181 (check_revocation) and line 287 (check_revocation_against_anchor): when `now_unix < this_update` the code returns `Err(OcspStatusUnknown)`. A future-dated `thisUpdate` is not a responder-reported unknown status — it means the SingleResponse is not yet valid (structurally invalid or clock skew). The parallel with `producedAt` is instructive: that case (line 176) correctly returns `OcspMalformed`. A future `thisUpdate` should also return `OcspMalformed` (or a dedicated `OcspNotYetValid`) not `OcspStatusUnknown`, which callers may interpret as a hard-fail on an authoritative 'unknown' answer from the responder. As written, a future-dated SingleResponse silently triggers the same hard-fail path as a responder saying 'I do not know this cert', which obscures the actual failure mode to callers and makes it impossible to distinguish clock-skew from a genuine responder-unknown. Suggested fix: change both checks to `return Err(Error::OcspMalformed)` (mirrors the producedAt treatment) or introduce an `OcspNotYetValid` error variant.
title: P0: thisUpdate future-date uses wrong error in OCSP
